Aston Martin Brings the CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Dreadnought Into the Real World, To Race It in Dakar
6 photos
Photo: Aston Martin
It rarely happens for a piece of news to keep me on my toes from start to finish, but that's exactly what Aston Martin's latest release managed to do this week. In a nutshell, the more I read, the more my eyes widened and my pulse accelerated, as this is more than a simple piece of news, it's a Christmas gift wrapped like a car.
Its name is Dreadnought , and it was first presented by the British carmaker back in July of this year. It didn't exist in the real world back then, as it was only created digitally to be included in the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 video game.
The digital Dreadnought, created with assistance from video game giants Infinity Ward and Activision, meant a great many things for Aston Martin, the most important of which being that it was its first-ever military-grade tactical SUV.
As such, it comes equipped with things Aston would never dream of fitting on its production cars: integrated weapons storage, adaptive combat zone intelligence systems, reserve fuel tanks, and tactical toggles to be used by players to raise bulletproof shields or call in airstrikes.
The SUV, which is powered by a digital V12 tied to an all-wheel drive system, is fully drivable in the game, and you probably only need to go online to see it in action, proving itself – I wouldn't know, I am actually a Battlefield guy.
{fullimg}
When it was presented a few months ago, nobody dreamed Aston would take the Dreadnought beyond the digital realm and the non-functional model shown at the Fanatics Fest NYC. Yet it is exactly what the carmaker announced this week – the piece of news that really got my blood pumping.
Long story short, the military-spec SUV from CoD will be officially brought into the physical world not to fight wars, but to take on the challenges of the 2027 Dakar race. There will not be a single one of them, but three.
Called just like the video game version, Dreadnought, the SUV does not exist in the real world in completed form yet, but it's getting pretty close, with British engineering crew Prodrive tasked with engineering, building, and racing it in the first couple of weeks of next year, alongside Aston Martin Racing.
All of the above means we don't have the specs of the design yet, but it doesn't mean there aren't more exciting things about it. Like, say, who has been tasked with getting behind the wheel of the Dreadnought and race it to the win, or as close as possible to that.
{fullimg}
As said, there will be three of these cars taking part in the endurance rally next year, and the British carmaker already knows who will be driving them: Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Team driver and two-time world champion, nine-time FIA World Rally champion Sebastien Loeb , and reigning FIA World Rally Raid champion Lucas Moraes.
Quite the lineup for what is officially Aston Martin Racing's first dive into the world of rally-raid, but despite that, the British crew won't have it easy. The premier prototype class of the competition where it will race will throw at it things made by some of the world's most powerful automotive houses.
It also happens to be one of the most challenging Dakar races in years, as in 2027 we'll be dealing with an entirely new route – a forced move, admittedly, caused by the conflicts in the area, but that won’t stop me from seeing the next Dakar as a breath of fresh air.
The 49th edition of the competition kicks off in Loule, Portugal, on January 9, with the prologue, and will get going a day later with the first special stage, which includes a transfer to the port of embarkation for Nador, Morocco.
{fullimg}
Following a night crossing of the Mediterranean Sea, teams will find themselves on the African continent on January 11, and they'll stand there until the finish, 12 stages and exactly two weeks later.
The 2027 Dakar race is scheduled to end in Marrakech, Morocco, on January 23, following 4,228 miles (6,805) of intense racing, of which 2,697 miles (4,341 km) are special stages.
We will keep an eye on Aston Martin and report back as soon as the Brits reveal more, including the technical details of the Dreadnought desert racer. Until then, you can enjoy it in the photos the carmaker released.
By the looks of it, we're only dealing with renderings of the vehicle, which in some cases appear to depict a Hot Wheels creation rather than a real-world Dakar contender, but that's probably not far from the way the ride will look once ready and presented in its physical form. And we probably don't have much waiting to do until that happens, seeing how the 2027 Dakar is less than two months away from the time of writing.
